status: Registered after mechanical/expert/complement development outcomes, before contact candidate scores
reason: Changing min duration alone gives essentially zero benefit; lower switch cost modestly increases short recall but not robust Spell F1. This points to insufficient short-control emission evidence. Test a different observable-contact mechanism rather than another duration/threshold sweep.
hypothesis: A close player moving with a continuously observed ball supplies additional evidence of brief control, while rejecting fast passes, stationary-ball restarts, uncertain opponents and gaps.
correction: Add signed log(9) to current H/A conditional log odds only where the contact gate passes. Never change missing coordinates or directly assign H/A/D. Keep geometry/period handling and all fitted weights fixed.
decoder_and_gap_options: Use only previously fixed original or .4s/4.5 short decoder and unchanged .75 neural/.25 activity gap blend. No new threshold or weight search after scoring.
data: All ten original development games, natural and fixed blind scenarios, both canonical and SDK references. No six-bridge, old-final or target data.
gate: Unchanged original recovery gate: +.02 mean Spell,8/10 wins,worst>=-.02,macro>=-.002 in each scenario/reference.
limitation: A deflection need not be possession. This is a hypothesis, not a hand-labelled control truth; any extra switches/erased true stoppages must remain visible. Reused adaptive development does not prove unseen improvement.
